paper.title_en: Unitarity bounds and sum rules in the SMEFT: a systematic analysis
paper.abstract_en: We present a systematic analysis of perturbative unitarity bounds and spinning sum rules in the baryon-number-conserving dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), with particular emphasis on flavor structure. Employing an on-shell partial-wave formalism for generic $N \to M$ scattering amplitudes, we perform a coupled-channel analysis of the complete operator basis and derive bounds on individual Wilson coefficients by marginalizing over the remaining interactions. We formulate spinning sum rules for four-fermion operators in the Warsaw basis and translate their flavor-space definiteness conditions into constraints on Wilson coefficients, under specified assumptions about the ultraviolet dynamics. We then extend both analyses to the three-generation four-fermion sector within Minimal Flavor Violation, retaining leading up-type Yukawa insertions, and an exact $U(2)^5$ flavor symmetry. The resulting constraints reveal correlations among flavor structures that are absent in the single-flavor limit. Through explicit matching to representative ultraviolet completions, we illustrate how spinning sum rules can distinguish scalar- from vector-mediated interactions, while also identifying the limitations of this interpretation. These results provide a general framework for assessing the consistency of new-physics scenarios within the SMEFT, relying on minimal theoretical assumptions.
